title: The letters, part 1: א to כ

steps.intro: Hebrew has 22 letters, all consonants. Here are words made only from the first eleven. Remember: start on the right.

cards.title: Aleph with Beth, lesson 7: the alphabet, part 1
cards.note: Optional: the letters spoken and written, taught in Biblical Hebrew. The next parts are listed in Videos.

cards.title: The first eleven letters
body: Each letter is a consonant. The vowels are the small marks added above and below, which the next lessons cover; for now, read the pronunciation under each word.
Learn each letter's sound with its name. Most names begin with the letter's own sound: bet starts with b, dalet with d.

head: letter
name
sound
rows: b, or v without the dot
k, or kh without the dot

cards.title: Letters that look alike
body: ב (bet) has a little foot at the bottom right; כ (kaf) is rounded with no foot.
ה (he) has a gap at the top left; ח (chet) is closed all round.
ו (vav) is a plain upright stroke; ז (zayin) has a little cap on top. י (yod) is the smallest letter, hanging high.

examples.en: bet has a foot; kaf doesn't
he has a gap; chet is closed
vav is plain; zayin has a cap

cards.title: A dot that changes the sound
body: A dot inside ב or כ makes the sound hard: בּ is b, ב is v; כּ is k, כ is kh. Grammar books call this dot a dagesh.
So אָב (father) ends in v, but בָּא (he came) starts with b. Four more letters take this dot; lesson 2 gives the full list.

examples.en: he came: b, with the dot

cards.explain: ב is bet: notice the little foot. כ, kaf, is rounded with no foot.
ח is a rough ch from the throat, as in loch. ה is the soft h.

cards.prompt: Match each letter to its sound.

cards.explain: Start on the right: י is y, then the vowel a, then ד is d: yad.

cards.prompt: Spell טוֹב (good), starting on the right.
cards.explain: ט (t), then וֹ (o), then ב (v): tov.
ד, ו, ד: da-VID. The name begins and ends with the same letter.

steps.intro: Real verses use all 22 letters, so don't expect to read every word yet. Look for the words you know.

cards.note: The last word, on the far left, is אֶחָד, one: “Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one.”
The verse ends with דָּוִד, David, the last of this family line.
